🇲🇽🏭 <u>Baja California Holds 4th Place in Mexico's Labor Market Ranking</u>

The 2026 State Competitiveness Index from IMCO, a business-friendly think tank that is no fan of the 4T, keeps Marina del Pilar's Baja California 4th nationwide on labor-market conditions. It cites formal employment, schooling and income levels. That puts the border state in the top tier with Baja California Sur, Mexico City and Jalisco.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum Weighs a Commercial Flight to China for APEC</u>

Mexico takes the APEC baton in 2028, after Vietnam in 2027, and Sheinbaum wants to be in China on November 18–19 to receive it. "It's our turn next, so presence matters," she said. The catch: about 24 hours of flying each way on a commercial airline, and she has to be back by dawn on the 20th to lead the Revolution Day parade.
banner: APEC IN CHINA: MEXICO HOSTS IN 2028

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Supreme Court Backs Vetting Candidates for Criminal Ties</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court upheld the electoral-law mechanism that lets parties and independent hopefuls request a risk assessment of possible links to organized crime before registering candidates. Security, intelligence, prosecution and financial authorities all feed into it. The Court ruled it does not violate the INE's autonomy. Results don't bar anyone from the ballot, but nobody can claim they weren't warned.
banner: SUPREME COURT OKS NARCO-VETTING OF CANDIDATES

🚨🇲🇽 <u>One in Three Migrants Dying in ICE Custody Is Mexican</u>

Since Trump returned in January 2025, 58 foreigners have died in ICE detention or during immigration operations. 18 of them, or 31%, were Mexican. Fiscal year 2026 closed with 37 deaths in custody, the deadliest in the agency's history. Mexico's Foreign Ministry has filed 20 complaints with US prosecutors and authorities demanding sanctions.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Dos Bocas Hits 270,000 Barrels a Day</u>

The refinery they called a white elephant ran at 79.41% of its 340,000-barrel capacity in August, according to Pemex data. That's 270,000 barrels a day, the first time since commercial operations began in 2024. Output is up 163.5% from August 2025, and diesel alone reached 106,000 barrels a day, just as Washington threatens to freeze diesel exports.

We are humanists and we are Mexicans." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 5, 2026 Asked why Latin America seems to be swinging right after Bolsonaro edged out Lula in Brazil's first round, Sheinbaum said she would only speak about Mexico. "The right is a political movement, an ideology that is against the people. It defends economic interests, the supremacy of some over others, racism, classism." In Mexico, she said, it resembles the 19th-century conservatives, the Porfiriato, the war on drugs, and treating education and health as commodities. "The people of Mexico always triumph over conservative movements."

text: 🚨🇲🇽 "It is very important to expose it and to say it, because if not, it becomes something normal, and it is not normal." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 5, 2026 Over the weekend, Querétaro governor Mauricio Kuri invited US Ambassador Ronald Johnson to lay the first stone of an international police training academy. The Defense Ministry, the federal Security Cabinet and the Foreign Ministry were not invited. "Any agency, any institution of the United States that wants to train in Mexico for security reasons has to go through the Foreign Ministry and the National Security Law." Sheinbaum asked the Foreign Minister to call both the ambassador and the governor. Did Kuri break the law? "Not so far, but it has to be named and said."
